title: LAB: First World War fighting, Western Front and Africa, 1914 to 1918 v0.1
snippet: Test map: move the time slider a month at a time to see where First World War fighting happened on the Western Front and across Africa, and the Western Front at the Armistice. Draft.
description:
Test map. Where fighting happened in the First World War, month by month from August 1914 to November 1918, on the Western Front and across Africa: Togoland, Kamerun, German South West Africa, East and Central Africa, North Africa, and risings against colonial rule.

Time slider: it steps one month at a time, landing on the 11th of each month, and ends on 11 November 1918. Large coloured symbols show fighting during that month. Small grey dots show fighting in earlier months. A battle shows for every month it was fought in, so a battle at the end of a month appears from that month's first step.

Symbols: circles are battles, sieges and raids; squares are captures and surrenders; diamonds are risings against colonial rule. The legend names each, so colour is not the only clue.

Western Front at the Armistice: the front line at 11 a.m. on 11 November 1918, traced from a US Army map of that day. It is usually within about 4 km of the map's line.

Where the points are: a battle fought over a wide area is shown at one place; the pop-up says where. Each pop-up names its source.

Sources: battle dates and facts from the National Army Museum, the American Battle Monuments Commission, The National Archives (UK), 1914-1918-online, London Gazette despatches and others named in each record. Front line: Order of Battle on Western Front, 11 A.M., Nov. 11, 1918, G-3, GHQ, American Expeditionary Forces (Library of Congress). Place positions: GeoNames.

Map version 0.1.1 (26 November 2026), lab draft.
